synopsis: Raw signal injection feeds simulated or recorded data into sensor electronics at a defined electrical interface; its evidential scope is determined by that boundary, with real downstream hardware tested but upstream components excluded [f13361, f5291, f5247]. Across the synthesis, sensor-testing chapter and glossary, the booklet consistently warns that injection cannot establish lens, imager, antenna or environmental performance, including contamination, vibration and glare; over-the-air stimulation exercises more of the real sensor front end [f96, f4498, f5296, f13037]. Camera injection can test downstream processing, bandwidth, timing, corrupted-frame handling and interface faults, and one vendor argues it avoids camera-box synchronization and field-of-view problems, although that argument is on-road vendor evidence [f13364, f5289]. Integration is sensor- and ECU-specific and ranked highest-effort: it requires the exact electrical/protocol interface, a realistic stream, synchronization and an adapter, making early confirmation of recording-format and data-rate compatibility important [f8641, f8731, f5292, f5669]. Every injection result should state its boundary, production injection ports must not remain open, and no current public heavy off-road standard prescribing an injection architecture for the listed positioning and infrastructure-aided systems was found [f13371, f5834, f5325].
